calls.head: Stars collide: O'Reilly vs. Horvat
calls.body: At home, the Predators keep sending O'Reilly’s line (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Islanders’ first line is Holmström, Horvat and Palmieri.
calls.call: The Predators’ L1 (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque) spends at least 51% of its 5-on-5 time against the Islanders’ first line, against about 38% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 64% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 38% with no line matching

chips.tip: Nashville’s L1 (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque) at home: 64% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Nashville home games this season, 6 games, 62 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 38% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Nashville’s L1 (Stamkos, O'Reilly, Bourque) spent 50% of its 5-on-5 time against the Islanders’ L1 (6:55 of 13:46). The call needed 51%, halfway from the 38% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 64%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque saw the Islanders’ first line some of the time
calls.plain: Nashville sent Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque out against the Islanders’ first line more than they would with no line matching, but not as often as the call needed.
calls.said: Andrew Brunette would send Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque out against the Islanders’ first line again

calls.head: The Predators kill penalties far better than the Islanders
calls.body: The Predators kill penalties well, but the Islanders don’t. Nashville is near the top of the league for the penalty kill, and the Islanders are one of the worst. Penalties should hurt the Islanders more than the Predators.
calls.call: The Predators’ penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Islanders’.

surprises.head: Nashville got the good looks
surprises.body: Nashville’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 10.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 300 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Schenn scores his 300th as the Islanders beat the Predators
paras: Anthony Duclair struck first for the Islanders early in the first, and Brayden Schenn scored his 300th NHL goal five minutes later to make it 2-0. Bo Horvat stretched the lead to 3-0 early in the second. Filip Forsberg and Alexander Kerfoot scored less than four minutes apart midway through the period to cut the Isles’ lead to 3-2. Ryan O'Reilly tied it 3-3 early in the third. Kyle Palmieri and Horvat scored in the shootout for the Islanders.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. It was Semyon Varlamov’s first NHL win since Nov 14, 2024. Juuse Saros kept the Predators in it, stopping 25 of 28. The Islanders moved to 6-4-2 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Predators dropped to 4-3-5, fifth in the Central.
